rv.q: Metcalf supplies the gravitation that holds it all together, even as her immense centrifugal energy is, simultaneously, working to fling it all apart.
Magnificent Metcalf, brief but deep psychological thriller

This is fearless acting, conveying the myriad painful human contradictions of a woman clinging to her formidable intellect like a life-raft while desperately trying to find a safe channel through the enveloping fog.
Thanks to the superb performance of Laurie Metcalf as Juliana, the less we are sure of, the more we are engaged.

The play — so buffed and polished it now seems to squeak — is matched by a searing, brilliant performance by Laurie Metcalf, who is simply astonishing as she goes from snippy, bossy scientist to a broken, confused intruder wolfing down Chinese food on the floor.
It is a breathtaking performance, but a wasted one.
Bold, unflinching, and ingeniously constructed, this is a show not to be missed.
It's crackling theater, and it elevates the puzzle-like structure of White's plot into something with real emotional heft.
Metcalf delivers a performance of such devastating honesty and raw emotional power that it's impossible to imagine anyone else in the role.
Like “The Great God Pan” earlier this season, “The Other Place” is yet another ambitious play that’s maddeningly unfinished.
The Other Place might lack poetry--or Wit--but its emotional moments are potent.

“The Other Place” satisfies and disturbs as it ties together the mystery involving Juliana’s daughter, and you’ll strain to wonder what goes through Metcalf’s mind, playing these particular moments opposite her own flesh-and-blood.
Metcalf, who earned an Obie Award in that earlier production, gives a performance as impressive for its elegance as it is for its fearlessness.
With all due respect to Metcalf, who never leaves the stage and gives a brave and raw performance, "The Other Place" leaves much to be desired.
With Metcalf's intense portrayal of a troubled doctor diluted in the much larger space, the work's contrivances and thinness are much more obvious.
